sample_unit: single mammographic views read by one radiologist
models_evaluated: PromptGate (client-adaptive biomedical vision-language model with site-specific learnable prompts)

links.outcome: Annotation queue purity with site-adaptive prompts versus static VLM filter and no filter
links.effect: Queue purity 92.5% with site-adaptive PromptGate vs 88.5% unfiltered and 87.0% static VLM filter; downstream density accuracy similar to unfiltered.
links.quote: Queue purity reached 92.5%, compared with 88.5% without filtering and 87.0% with a static vision-language model filter, while downstream density accuracy remained similar to the unfiltered condition.

unlisted_practices: Using an AI gatekeeper to filter out irrelevant artifact images from clinician annotation queues in federated learning to reduce annotation time

screen.reason: Empirically tests an automated vision-language gatekeeper/filter designed to remove unsuitable artifact-containing images from a radiologist's annotation queue, measuring clinician reading time, queue purity, and label reliability.

primary.practice: vision-language input gatekeeper / artifact filtering for clinician annotation queue
